topic_title: 13C NMR — Broadband Decoupled and DEPT Logic

notes_list.title: 13C NMR — Broadband Decoupled and DEPT Logic
notes_list.basic_overview: 13C NMR distinguishes chemically different carbon environments and is commonly acquired with broadband proton decoupling. DEPT experiments help classify CH, CH2 and CH3 carbons.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Signal count approximates unique carbon environments. Proton-decoupled spectra collapse 13C–1H coupling, while DEPT phase behavior differentiates protonated carbon classes.
notes_list.examples: DEPT-135: CH and CH3 commonly appear with one phase while CH2 appears opposite; quaternary carbons are absent. Exact phase convention depends on display setup.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Broadband decoupling improves spectral simplicity but reduces direct coupling information. DEPT requires pulse-sequence control and appropriate acquisition parameters.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Use molecular symmetry to predict signal count; compare carbonyl, aromatic, alkene and aliphatic chemical-shift regions.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Signal intensity is not directly proportional to carbon count because NOE, relaxation and acquisition conditions affect peak intensities.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not count peaks as atoms without considering symmetry and accidental overlap.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
